title: CILIARY DYSKINESIA, PRIMARY, 2
alt_titles: CILIARY DYSKINESIA, PRIMARY, 2, WITH OR WITHOUT SITUS INVERSUS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that primary ciliary dyskinesia-2 (CILD2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DNAAF3 gene on chromosome 19q13.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia-2 (CILD2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DNAAF3 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We detected homozygous mutations in DNAAF3 in two of the three originally linked families (UCL66/67 and UCL89)
checks.explanation: Homozygous DNAAF3 mutations found in CILD2-linked families.

checks.claim: The DNAAF3 gene is located on chromosome 19q13.
checks.evidence_quote: The human DAB1 orthologous gene DNAAF3 on human chromosome 19q13 (previously designated C19orf51) encodes a 588 amino acid protein

paragraphs.text: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is an autosomal recessive disorder with chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility. Situs inversus is present in about half of cases (Kartagener syndrome). The clinical features result from defective ciliary function, which is associated with ultrastructural abnormalities such as absent dynein arms, absent radial spokes, and disturbed ciliary orientation (Meeks et al., 2000). CILD2 is caused by mutation in DNAAF3, a cytoplasmic factor needed to preassemble axonemal dyneins. Patients have immotile respiratory cilia that lack both outer and inner dynein arms (Mitchison et al., 2012).

checks.evidence_quote: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive condition

checks.evidence_quote: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive condition characterised by chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) studied 10 patients with PCD and DNAAF3 mutations from 3 families. Two of the families were consanguineous and of Arabic origin; the third (UCL71) was a UK-Pakistani family from a first-cousin union. The parents of all affected individuals except 2 were first cousins. All of the families had classic clinical symptoms of PCD: neonatal respiratory distress, recurrent cough and wheezing, nasal discharge and chest infections, sinusitis, otitis media, nasal polyps, and bronchiectasis. Four of the 10 affected individuals had situs inversus. One family (UCL89) included affected monozygotic twins. In nasal brushing biopsies, cilia were immotile in all affected family members. Where electron microscopy of respiratory cilia was available, it showed a shared defect of reduced or absent inner and outer dynein arms. Mitchison et al. (2012) concluded that loss of DNAAF3 gives rise to classical PCD with defective left-right organ asymmetry and male infertility.

checks.evidence_quote: Clinical features of the 10 patients carrying DNAAF3 mutations are detailed in Supplementary Table 2.
checks.explanation: Three families (UCL66/67, UCL89, UCL71) with 10 patients.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) used immunofluorescence on nasal brushing samples from patients with DNAAF3 mutations. The outer dynein arm proteins DNAH5, DNAH9, and DNAI2 and the inner dynein arm light chain DNALI1 were all absent from the patients' cilia. This indicated that assembly of outer dynein arm types 1 and 2 and of DNALI1-containing inner dynein arms was disrupted along the full length of the axoneme. In some patient cells, residual DNAH5 and DNALI1 were seen in the apical cytoplasm, which was not seen in control cells.

checks.evidence_quote: Respiratory cells obtained by nasal-brushing biopsy from DNAAF3 patients were analyzed for expression of ODA proteins DNAH5, DNAH9, DNAI2

checks.claim: The outer dynein arm proteins DNAH5, DNAH9, and DNAI2 were absent from the cilia of patients with DNAAF3 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: ODA components DNAH5 (Fig. 3), DNAH9 and DNAI2 (see Supplementary Fig. 3 and 4), and IDA light chain DNALI1 (Fig. 4) were all absent from the cilia of affected patients.

checks.claim: The inner dynein arm light chain DNALI1 was absent from the cilia of patients with DNAAF3 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: ODA components DNAH5 (Fig. 3), DNAH9 and DNAI2 (see Supplementary Fig. 3 and 4), and IDA light chain DNALI1 (Fig. 4) were all absent from the cilia of affected patients.

checks.claim: In patients with DNAAF3 mutations, assembly of outer dynein arm types 1 and 2 and of DNALI1-containing inner dynein arms was disrupted along the full length of the axoneme.
checks.evidence_quote: These results suggest that DNAAF3 is important for the assembly of outer and inner dynein arms along the entire length of the axoneme, comprising ODA types 1 and 2 and the DNALI1 containing IDA types.

checks.evidence_quote: In some patients, residual DNAH5 and DNALI1 can be seen in the apical cytoplasm, whereas cytoplasmic accumulation of these proteins is not seen in control samples.

paragraphs.text: Meeks et al. (2000) performed a genome scan in 5 Arabic families with PCD. Using GENEHUNTER, they obtained a maximum multipoint lod score (HLOD) of 4.4 on chromosome 19q13.3-qter at an alpha (proportion of linked families) of 0.7. Recombinations at D19S572 and D19S218 defined a 15-cM critical region.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) sequenced DNAAF3, which lies within the CILD2 locus on chromosome 19q13, in consanguineous Arabic-origin PCD families previously linked to this locus. Two of the 3 originally linked families had homozygous mutations; in both, affected individuals had large regions of marker homozygosity spanning DNAAF3. Family UCL89 carried a missense mutation (L108P) and family UCL66/67 carried a nonsense mutation (R136X). Neither variant was found on 148 population-matched control Arabic chromosomes.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) then sequenced DNAAF3 in 112 more PCD families. Of these, 107 had outer dynein arm defects and 9 had evidence for linkage to the chromosome 19 locus. One linked family (UCL71), a UK-Pakistani first-cousin union, was homozygous for a 1-bp insertion that was predicted to cause a frameshift and premature termination (V255CfsTer12). This variant was absent from 172 control UK-Pakistani chromosomes. A Belgian patient was homozygous for an ala325-to-thr (A325T) substitution. However, this variant was found on 1 of 192 Caucasian control chromosomes, was predicted to be benign, and affected a nonconserved residue, so it was considered likely to be a Caucasian polymorphism. For the 3 pathogenic mutations, all affected individuals were homozygous and unaffected parents and sibs were heterozygous. None of the 3 mutations was found in the dbSNP, 1000 Genomes, or NHLBI-ESP databases.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) found that the Chlamydomonas reinhardtii pf22 mutant, which is nonmotile and has paralyzed half-length flagella, carries a nonsense mutation (trp79-to-ter) in DAB1, the ortholog of DNAAF3. The resulting flagellar defects were rescued by transformation with the wildtype gene. The pf22 mutant failed to assemble outer dynein arms and inner dynein arms 'b' and 'c', but retained inner arm 'f'. Tagged PF22 protein was found only in the cytoplasm. In pf22 cytoplasm, outer arm heavy chain levels were near normal, but intermediate chain IC2 was hyperabundant. Heavy chain trypsin sensitivity was less strongly altered in pf22 than in the pf13 and oda7 mutants. Immunoprecipitation showed that dynein complexes formed in pf22 cytoplasm but had abnormal properties, including a buried HC-beta epitope and a reduced amount of HC-gamma. Mitchison et al. (2012) suggested that PF22 acts at a later step of cytoplasmic dynein preassembly than PF13 and ODA7.

checks.evidence_quote: The Chlamydomonas pf22 strain was previously shown to be non-motile, with paralyzed half-length flagella and disrupted ODA assembly.

checks.claim: Mitchison et al. (2012) found that the Chlamydomonas pf22 mutant carries a nonsense mutation (trp79-to-ter) in DAB1.
checks.evidence_quote: The Chlamydomonas pf22 mutant DAB1 gene has a single G to A base change in exon 3 at codon 79, TGG -> TGA, altering a tryptophan to a nonsense codon (p.Trp79X)

checks.evidence_quote: The human DAB1 orthologous gene DNAAF3 on human chromosome 19q13

checks.evidence_quote: Transforming a 7.2 kb genomic fragment spanning a single gene rescued the pf22 phenotype (short flagella, lack of motility and dynein assembly defect) to wild-type

checks.evidence_quote: IDA dyneins “b” (DHC5) and “c” (DHC9) fail to assemble in pf22 axonemes, whereas dimeric IDA dynein “f” (DIC140) is retained

checks.evidence_quote: Heavy chain tryptic sensitivity is less strongly altered in pf22, and the pattern of sites sensitive to digestion did not change, therefore if PF22 acts as a co-chaperone, it likely works at a later step than PF13 and ODA7

checks.claim: Immunoprecipitation showed that dynein complexes formed in Chlamydomonas pf22 cytoplasm but had abnormal properties.
checks.evidence_quote: these results show that complexes can form in the pf22 cytoplasm, but an epitope on the HCβ tail that is normally exposed is buried as a consequence of the loss of PF22 function

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) knocked down dnaaf3 in zebrafish with morpholinos. Morphant embryos had immotile olfactory placode cilia with reduced or missing outer and inner dynein arms. Other phenotypes included body axis curvature (64% and 78% of embryos with the 2 splice-blocking morpholinos), hydrocephalus (18% and 34%), pronephric cysts, abnormal otolith number, and reduced and disorganized beating of pronephric and spinal cord cilia. About half of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos had reversed heart looping or no heart looping.

checks.evidence_quote: We determined the effects of dnaaf3 loss during zebrafish development by gene silencing, using antisense morpholinos

checks.evidence_quote: including completely static olfactory placode cilia, as illustrated by high speed video microscopy

checks.evidence_quote: electron microscopy revealed abnormal ultrastructure including reduced or missing ODAs and IDAs (Fig. 5)

checks.evidence_quote: was observed in 64% of dnaaf3MOex3 and 78% of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos
checks.explanation: MOex3 and MOex8 are the splice-blocking morpholinos.

checks.evidence_quote: Hydrocephalus was also present in 18% of dnaaf3MOex3 and 34% of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos

checks.evidence_quote: Pronephric cysts developed progressively in dnaaf3MOex8 embryos from 2 dpf (49%) to 5 dpf (77%)

checks.evidence_quote: While control embryos invariably had two otoliths, 27% of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos had 1-3 otoliths, which often appeared malformed

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a consanguineous Arabic-origin family (UCL89) with primary ciliary dyskinesia-2, Mitchison et al. (2012) identified a homozygous c.323T-C transition in exon 3 of the DNAAF3 gene, resulting in a leu108-to-pro (L108P) substitution at a residue that is highly conserved across ciliated species. The affected family members included monozygotic twins. Unaffected parents and sibs were heterozygous for the mutation. The mutation was absent from 148 population-matched control Arabic chromosomes and from the dbSNP, 1000 Genomes, and NHLBI-ESP databases, and PolyPhen-2 and SIFT predicted it to be damaging. Respiratory cilia from affected individuals lacked outer and inner dynein arms on electron microscopy, lacked DNAH5 and DNALI1 on immunofluorescence, and were immotile.

(2012) identified a homozygous c.406C-T transition in exon 4 of the DNAAF3 gene, resulting in an arg136-to-ter (R136X) substitution. Unaffected parents and sibs were heterozygous for the mutation. The mutation was absent from 148 population-matched control Arabic chromosomes and from the dbSNP, 1000 Genomes, and NHLBI-ESP databases.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a UK-Pakistani family (UCL71) from a first-cousin union with primary ciliary dyskinesia-2, Mitchison et al. (2012) identified a homozygous 1-bp insertion (c.762_763insT) in exon 6 of the DNAAF3 gene. The insertion was predicted to cause a val255-to-cys substitution followed by a frameshift that adds 11 novel amino acids before a premature stop codon (V255CfsTer12). Unaffected parents and sibs were heterozygous for the mutation. The mutation was absent from 172 control UK-Pakistani chromosomes and from the dbSNP, 1000 Genomes, and NHLBI-ESP databases.
